Yes, that is so.
When on earth did things turn out like this? Really, since when?

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: なんでそこまで俺を拒否すんだよ？
examples.trans: Why are you rejecting me to this extent?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: ほとんどの女優が撮影拒否のストライキ状態。
examples.trans: Nearly all the actresses are refusing to shoot, practically on strike.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 未払い金払ってもらうまでやめな。
examples.trans: Don't shoot another frame until they pay your back wages.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 金さえ払えば、村西さんは釈放される。
examples.trans: As long as we pay the money, Muranishi will be released.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: nothing more than (after past verb); up to
meanings.note: After a plain verb + です (出店したまでです), modestly states 'we simply did that and nothing more'.

examples.text: 念のため聞いたまでです。
examples.trans: I merely asked just in case.

meanings.en: bring to a halt; shut off
meanings.note: Transitive verb for stopping a car, engine, or machine.

examples.text: ここに車を止めてください。
エンジンを止めました。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for one's job or workplace duties.

examples.text: 新しい仕事は楽しいです。
これから仕事に行きます。
examples.trans: I am heading to work now.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

examples.text: それに私、モデルのお仕事なんかも始めましたので。
examples.trans: Besides, I've also started doing modelling work.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: もう別現場で仕事し始めてるよ。監督とメイクの仕事も少しずつ増えてきたし。
examples.trans: I've already started working on other sets, and directing and makeup jobs are picking up.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Intransitive ichidan verb meaning something increases in number or amount.

examples.text: 最近お客さんが増えました。
仕事が増えて忙しくなりました。
examples.trans: Work increased and I got busy.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Attached to names of children, close friends, or familiar acquaintances.

examples.text: トシちゃん、また来たの？

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: 村西監督、テレビ出演おめでとう！
examples.trans: Director Muranishi, congratulations on your television appearance!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Interrogative pronoun for time.

examples.text: いつまでも待っています。

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Na-adjective; 簡単に means 'easily'.

examples.text: そう簡単に売れないよ。

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Filler or polite attention-getter.

examples.text: あの、ちょっとよろしいですか。
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

examples.text: あの、実は相談があります。
examples.trans: Um, actually I have something to ask you.

meanings.en: respectful word for a person (かた)
meanings.note: Read かた, polite replacement for 人 (ひと) when announcing visitors or customers.

examples.text: あの方はどなたですか。

examples.trans: The person in charge has arrived.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: 簡単ですわ。あの方がご自身をポルノの帝王と思わなくなった瞬間からです。
examples.trans: It is simple—from the moment he stopped thinking of himself as the emperor of porn.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: その瞬間を待っていた。
examples.trans: I was waiting for that moment.

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。
ちょっと見せてください。これぐらいの金額だったら多分…
examples.trans: Let me take a look at that. With an amount around this size, maybe...

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Reassures that rules or steps are followed properly.

examples.text: ちゃんと確認しました。
ちゃんと並んでいます。

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: もう少しよく考えてみます。
examples.trans: I'll think about it a little more carefully.

meanings.note: I-adjective; after て-form (～てほしい), means 'want someone to do something'.

examples.trans: I want you to come soon.

examples.text: 諦めてほしくないのです。
examples.trans: I don't want you to give up.

meanings.note: Connects a contrasting fact or trails off at the end of a sentence to voice a polite objection.

examples.text: お風呂に入りましたけど。
examples.trans: I already took a bath, though.

examples.text: 高いけど、おいしいです。

meanings.note: Softens a refusal or correction at the start of a reply.
Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').

examples.text: いや、監督も今走り回ってますから。
examples.trans: Look, the director is running all over town right now trying to fix this.

examples.text: 走り回ってるんじゃなくて逃げ回ってるんだろ！
examples.trans: He's not running around working—he's running away!

meanings.note: Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Ichidan verb; potential form 信じられる means 'can believe' (信じられない = unbelievable).

examples.text: あなたの言葉を信じます。
そんなこと、信じられません。
examples.trans: I can't believe such a thing.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: With します, forms お願いします ('please'), the standard polite way to request a service or favor.

examples.text: 一つお願いがあります。
examples.trans: I have one favor to ask.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
